notes: RECORD 4 OF 6, AND THE ONE THE TRAP WARNING WAS WRITTEN FOR. The register's bare 'Confirmed' hides a Commission REJECTION (21 March 1854) reversed by the U.S. District Court (decree stamped PAGE 48, filed 26 Nov 1855). Graded OK only because the reversing decree itself was read verbatim, not inferred: stopping at the Commission would have produced a false ERR here, exactly as stopping there elsewhere produces a false OK. | ONE LOOSE END, FLAGGED NOT GUESSED: on 13 Jan 1857 the court granted the United States an appeal to the SUPREME COURT from its own final decision (order, stamped PAGE 50, image 63: 'an appeal in behalf of the United States from the final decision of this Court rendered in said Cause at the June Term 1855 be, and the same is hereby granted, and that a certified transcript... be sent to the Supreme Court of the United States without delay'). I did not read the disposition of that appeal. It is not treated as doubt about the outcome because everything later in this same file presupposes the confirmation stood: the 1859-60 proceedings are all about LOCATING the confirmed tract (survey objections, stamped PAGE 62, image 75; Hoffman's order of 3 Dec 1859, stamped PAGE 72, image 85; Jeremiah Clarke's intervention, stamped PAGE 102, image 115, which recites 'said survey is erroneous and does not conform to the decree of confirmation heretofore made herein'). Phase C should still confirm the Supreme Court appeal was dismissed. | MARIA ANTONIA MESA WAS ALREADY DEAD when the claim was decided: the District Court petition, stamped PAGE 42 (image 55), recites that 'on the 10th day of January A.D. 1854 the said cause was by the order of said Board revived and ordered to be prosecuted in the names of the heirs of said Maria Antonia Mesa upon the suggestion & proof of her death', and the decree is captioned 'Antonia Maria Meza (Heirs of)'. The register's patent_to 'Maria Antonia Mesa' with a patent date of 1872 therefore names a woman dead nearly twenty years; Phase C should check whether GLO 147 issued to her heirs. notes: RECORD 6 OF 6. THE STRONGEST POSITIVE CONTROL IN THE CHUNK ON THE AUDIT'S DOMINANT ERROR CLASS. This is the case where writing the U.S.-era claimant into the grantee field would have been easiest and most tempting: the binding, the transcript title page and the whole litigation are in the name of Captain JOSEPH L. FOLSOM, and Leidesdorff never appears as a party because he died 18 May 1848. The register nonetheless carries Leidesdorff, exactly as the titulo does. The chain is set out in the petition, stamped PAGE 7 (image 13): Leidesdorff died leaving 'one parent surviving, to wit, his Mother, Anna Maria Spark of the Island of Santa Cruz in the Danish West Indies who was his sole heir'; Spark sold to Folsom on 17 Sept 1849, and the supplementary petition, stamped PAGE 9 (image 15), asks that the land 'may be Confirmed to the petitioner Joseph L. Folsom who is now the sole owner thereof'. The Commission confirmed to Folsom; the GRANT was to Leidesdorff. Register right. | HAD TO GO PAST THE 30-PAGE CAP TO GRADE THIS HONESTLY. The front matter (stamped pp.1-27) is entirely petitions and depositions; the register's values are recited in the claim petition at stamped PAGE 7, but the method forbids grading off the petition, and Sutter's authentication of Micheltorena's signature (stamped PAGE 13, image 20) is testimony. The expediente itself sits at stamped pp.43-50 (Spanish) with the sworn translation at pp.50-59, roughly PDF images 50-68, which no 30-page front read would reach. FOR OTHER AGENTS: in this transcript the grant papers are NOT near the front; look around stamped p.43. | TWO GRANT DATES, BOTH 1844, NO CONFLICT: Micheltorena's concession is endorsed 'Granted' on 1 Oct 1844 (translation, stamped PAGE 50) and the formal titulo is dated 8 Oct 1844 (Spanish, stamped PAGE 47). The claim petition (stamped PAGE 7) compresses this into 'On the eighth day of October A.D. 1844 decreed to said Leidesdorff', which is the titulo date, not the concession date. Anyone recording a precise grant DAY for this rancho should use the decree, not the petition. | REGISTER'S OWN INTERNAL GAP, FOR PHASE C: this row has patent_date 'Oct. 28, 1864' and glo_patent_no '98' filled in but patent_to and patent_acres BLANK, the only such row in this chunk. Folsom died in 1855, so the patentee is likely his estate or devisees; worth resolving from GLO. Left null here per method. | Do not confuse stamped PAGE 64 (image 73) with this grant: it is a copy of SUTTER's New Helvetia titulo ('once sitios de ganado mayor', latitude 39.41.45 north, bounded by the Rio de las Plumas and the Rio Sacramento), filed as evidence of the adjoining boundary. | Image = stamped page + 4 at the front, drifting to +7 by stamped p.43 and +10 by stamped p.80.
